reasoning_traces.think:
NRI models multi-agent systems by jointly learning an interaction graph and a dynamical model from observed trajectories. It uses a variational autoencoder where the latent variable z represents the interaction graph, and the decoder is a graph neural network (GNN). The encoder processes trajectory data to estimate posterior over z, while the decoder generates future states conditioned on z. This dual learning enables unsupervised discovery of relational structures like defensive coverage patterns in basketball. For GSE, this translates into real-time tactical inference from tracking data, where man-to-man and zone coverage are treated as distinct graph topologies. The GNN decoder allows prediction of next-state player positions, enabling situational awareness and strategic planning. The key insight is that relational structure—such as who defends whom—is not directly observed but emerges from the temporal evolution of player trajectories. The model's strength lies in its ability to generalize across domains (physics, motion capture, basketball) due to shared relational structure. Failure modes include poor generalization when interaction graphs are too complex or when data lacks sufficient temporal resolution to distinguish between interaction types.
